tasks.short: Talk with colleagues and counsellors about a student's problem, share information and follow up by e-mail and phone, look up earlier incidents and agreements, and note new agreements in the student's file.

steps.what: Residential advisor communicates with other staff to resolve problems with individual students
Residential advisor e-mails and phones staff to share information and follow up
Residential advisor looks up the student's earlier incidents and agreements
Residential advisor notes agreements in the student's file

tasks.design: Each student with a problem gets a case in the residence system ({OTHER}) with earlier incidents, agreements and follow-up tasks visible to the staff involved, so information is not passed by e-mail chains and tasks do not get lost. Access is limited to staff who need it. Talking with colleagues and deciding what to do stay with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information sat in e-mails and notebooks of different staff.
tasks.enabler_now: Residence systems hold student cases with tasks and access rights.
tasks.still_hard: Staff work different shifts and miss each other.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the pattern behind a student's repeated small problems.

reach.learn: Whether cases are handed over complete.

evidence.claim: Residence systems can hold student cases with follow-up tasks and access rights.
Notes on students' health are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student problem to agreements noted; counselling is outside.
Input contract: incidents and agreements kept in the residence system; fallback is e-mail and notebooks.
Talks with colleagues do not change.
Colleagues use the case as they would e-mail.
research_questions: Do follow-up tasks get done more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few problem cases; high: a large hall with many cases and staff.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe students in the hall, decide whether behavior is unusual and write an incident report, send it to the residence manager, and talk with the student or counsellor about serious cases.

steps.what: Residential advisor observes students to detect unusual behavior
Residential advisor decides whether the behavior seen is unusual
Residential advisor writes an incident report with type, place and what happened
Residential advisor e-mails the report to the residence manager
Residential advisor talks with the student or counsellor about serious cases

tasks.design: Incident reports are a short form on the advisor's phone in the residence system ({OTHER}) with type, place and what happened; once the advisor has written it, it goes to the residence manager. Observing students and judging what is unusual stay with the advisor; no camera or software analyses students' behavior.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were typed at the end of the shift and e-mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Phone incident forms are common in residence systems.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a student who stopped coming to the shared kitchen.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive the same night.

evidence.claim: Residence systems offer phone incident forms that route to a manager.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from residents to the case followed up; disciplinary decisions are outside.
Input contract: report form set by the residence office; fallback is typed reports.
Observing and talking with students do not change.
research_questions: Do managers act on incidents sooner?

incremental.description: Residential advisor learns the incident form.

approvals.approved_version: The incident report as written by the advisor in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few incidents; high: a large hall with many reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make the duty roster, supervise and coach residence hall staff, train new resident assistants, write evaluations, sign them, send them to the housing office, and approve student workers' hours.

steps.what: Residential advisor makes the duty roster in a spreadsheet
Residential advisor supervises residence hall staff and student workers
Residential advisor trains new resident assistants
Residential advisor evaluates the work of each staff member and student worker
Residential advisor writes evaluations of staff and student workers on the form
Residential advisor checks and signs the evaluations
Residential advisor e-mails the evaluations to the housing office
Residential advisor approves work-study students' hours on paper timesheets

tasks.design: Resident assistants enter their availability in a scheduling tool ({CALENDAR}) that builds the duty roster within set rules, and worked hours from the roster go to payroll ({PAYROLL}) for the advisor to approve. Policy and safety modules for new assistants move to the learning system ({LMS}), so training time goes to practice. Evaluation forms in the HR system ({HCM}) are written by the advisor and, once signed, filed there. Supervising and coaching stay with the advisor; roster data are not used to rate staff without works council consent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rosters were built in spreadsheets, timesheets were paper and policies taught in person.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling tools, learning systems and HR forms are standard in universities.
tasks.still_hard: Student workers' availability changes with exams.
tasks.human_edge: Coaching a new assistant after a hard night on duty.

reach.learn: Whether rosters are fairer and more stable.

evidence.claim: Scheduling tools build rosters from availability; learning systems deliver policy modules.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff availability to hours approved; hiring is outside.
Input contract: availability from assistants; policy modules from the housing office; fallback is spreadsheets and paper.
Supervising, coaching and judging do not change.
Assistants enter availability in about the time a message took.

incremental.description: Residential advisor keeps roster rules and modules current.

approvals.approved_version: The evaluations as checked and signed by the advisor in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small team; high: many student workers with changing availability.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk regular rounds through the halls, record findings in the logbook, and report defects to facilities.

steps.what: Residential advisor makes regular rounds to ensure residents and areas are safe and secure
Residential advisor records round findings in the logbook
Residential advisor reports defects to facilities by phone or e-mail

tasks.design: Round findings go into a phone form with pick lists, and a defect seen on the round becomes a ticket for the facilities desk ({HELPDESK}) from the same form with a photo. Walking the rounds and judging what is unsafe stay with the advisor. The form logs findings, not the advisor's route or times, unless the works council agrees.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings were written in a paper logbook and defects reported by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Phone forms and facilities ticket desks are common.
tasks.still_hard: Safety issues at night need action, not a ticket.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a quiet corridor is too quiet.

reach.learn: Whether defects come with photos and places.

evidence.claim: Phone forms can log round findings and open facilities tickets with photos.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the round schedule to defects reported; repairs are outside.
Input contract: facilities desk takes tickets; fallback is the logbook and phone.

incremental.description: Residential advisor checks open tickets on the next round.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few findings per round; high: an old building with many defects.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The residential advisor keeps talking with staff and students, observing, supervising and walking rounds; e-mail chains, paper logbooks and spreadsheet rosters shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An advisor with more time among residents.
